shortcut_name: uniform same-mode constraints reduce to bipartite coloring
evidence: deepseek uses `color = [0] * n`, `try assigning color 1 to start`, and a BFS; gpt-oss, qwen3-coder, and glm-5 all explicitly hard-code the two matrices and implement 4x4 multiplication to classify their products.
affordance_in_statement: Each instance's matrix is determined only by whether its mode is 1 or 2, and every backup array requires that `neither M_u × M_v nor M_v × M_u may equal Z`.
removal_suggestion: Break the uniform two-matrix compatibility pattern: make the transformation matrix depend on the instance as well as its mode, or otherwise specify an index-dependent perturbation for instances outside the examples, so an edge is no longer characterized solely by whether its endpoint modes are equal.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the constraints as ordinary two-coloring and solves each component by BFS.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The two fixed modes and the fixed zero-product pattern make every edge require opposite colors.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Computes the four fixed mode-pair products once, then reduces the resulting uniform edge constraint to graph coloring.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement supplies the same two matrices for every instance and defines constraints only through endpoint matrix products.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly multiplies the two fixed matrices and uses the resulting pair compatibility to perform bipartite-style assignment.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Every vertex has only one of two globally identical matrix choices.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Hard-codes the two matrices, classifies zero products, and applies the resulting two-color graph constraint.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The bidirectional product condition is uniform for every input edge.

common_affordance: All vertices use one of the same two globally fixed matrices, so every edge has the same mode-pair compatibility table and the constraints collapse to bipartite coloring.
recommended_edit: Change the matrix rule from globally fixed mode matrices to instance-dependent matrices—for example, retain the published matrices for the first four instances so the examples remain valid, but define an index-dependent transformation for later instances. Keep the same input and output formats and the same bidirectional nonzero-product requirement.
